references.text: Jesus uses the same word to warn the disciples against 'grumbling' (γογγύζετε) when they are offended by his teaching, which directly mirrors the warning in 6:43.
Here the Lord warns Moses about the people who 'grumbled' (γογγύζω) against him and Moses, a pattern Jesus refers to when he warns against grumbling against himself.
During the Korah rebellion, the people grumbled against Moses and Aaron, a directly parallel motif to the people grumbling against Jesus in John 6.
The psalm describes how the people 'grumbled' (γογγύζω) in their tents, a historical example of the kind of resistance Jesus addresses in his message.
Paul warns against 'grumbling' (γογγύζω) as some of the Israelites did, and links this directly to the same events in the wilderness that underlie Jesus' warning.
Jude warns against those who 'grumble' (γογγύζω) and complain, drawing parallels to the wilderness generation, which resonates with Jesus' warning in John 6.
